D3·6rk8 — 2026-09-15
rule: Private diagnostics live only under the XDG state dir keyed by clone hash, never under the repo or .sofar/.index; every exporter, push and pull path must be pinned by a sentinel test proving it moves none of them.
chose: 1.1(b) — the diagnostics STORAGE BOUNDARY, gating 1.2.
(1) Location: OUTSIDE the repo. Private diagnostics live under `~/.local/state/sofar/diagnostics/<sha256(clone-path)>/` (XDG_STATE_HOME-aware), keyed exactly like the sync cursors in sync-client D2's storage triad. Never under `.sofar/`, never under the clone root; the path resolver refuses a target inside the repo and a test pins that refusal.
(2) Form: an append-only JSONL journal of rows in the packages/schema/src row shape, one file per initiative slug, each row stamped with schema version, engine version, clone hash, initiative, session id, timestamp, kind, host tool and version when known. Rotated at a per-clone byte cap; rows older than 90 days deleted on the next write; a purge subcommand wipes the clone's store. Exact cap and names are settled in 1.2 against measured row sizes.
(3) Not truth, not derived. The store is a THIRD class next to events.jsonl (truth) and .sofar/.index (derived, disposable): raw observations that exist nowhere else and are NOT rebuildable, so it never goes in .index (record-index D1 forbids irrebuildable data there) and never claims disposability. Its loss costs evidence, never record correctness — nothing the fold, the projections or the digest's byte-stable block depends on may read it.
(4) The exemption does not reach it. record-hygiene D1 exempts git and sofar commands from the RECORD because the append would keep the tree from settling; the store is outside the tree, so exempt commands and read-only MCP calls ARE counted there (command token only, redacted). This recovers the bookkeeping-share denominator the audit (S1) called unmeasurable — with coverage limits 1.3 must state: hooks fire only on Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash, MCP calls are counted by the server itself, and Read/Grep/other tools are never observed.
(5) Best-effort per BD22, and never recursive: a failed row write never fails the user's tool call, never appends an event, and is never itself recorded as a diagnostic. MCP typed-error rejections write a row and still append nothing to the record (no-write-on-invalid-input is pinned by test).
(6) Enforced at the boundary by tests: with a seeded store carrying a sentinel under a fake XDG_STATE_HOME, exportEvents, exportNDJSON, `sofar export`, pushStream (mock fetch) and pullStream/importNDJSON must move zero bytes of it; a row must fail validateEnvelope; a row write in a temp repo must leave `git status` clean.
(7) Sanitized evidence: a proposal (2.3) may carry row ids, hashes and counts into the record as its evidence; when the rows have expired the consumer reports evidence unavailable, never reconstructs it.
over: (a) `.sofar/.diagnostics/` with a self-ignoring `.gitignore` of `*`, the .index pattern, which is what the task text literally says ("gitignored"). (b) Appending diagnostics as events to events.jsonl with an export-time type filter. (c) A new tier inside `.sofar/.index/`.
because: Verified against main @ b29d013: exportEvents/pushStream read only `.sofar/initiatives/<slug>/events.jsonl` and filter by envelope validity and cursor, never by type — so (b) would need a filter in every present and future exporter, and one missed path leaks. (c) is ruled out by record-index D1: every .index file must be deletable and rebuildable, and raw observations are neither. (a) satisfies the wording but rests on one file staying present: `git add -f`, a deleted .gitignore, `npm pack` of a repo without the private flag, or a worktree copy each defeat it, and the self-improve D1 rule is absolute. A path outside the clone is uncommittable, unpackable and unexportable by construction, and the repo already keeps per-clone state there (sync cursors), so no new convention is introduced. The cost is real and accepted: deleting the repo strands the store, hence the 90-day retention and purge; and diagnostics are per machine, which is correct for evidence that describes this machine's sessions. Counting exempt commands there is safe because the exemption's only purpose (a settleable tree) is untouched.
